lessons.title: Fertiliser and the macadamia tree
lessons.html:
Why trees need fertiliser

A macadamia tree takes food from the soil to grow leaves, flowers and nuts. Every harvest takes food out of the orchard. Fertiliser puts food back. The main plant foods are:

  • Nitrogen (N) – for green leaves and new growth.
  • Phosphorus (P) – for roots.
  • Potassium (K) – for filling the nuts.
  • Others such as calcium, magnesium, boron and zinc, needed in smaller amounts.

Who decides how much?

The farm takes soil and leaf samples and sends them to a laboratory. The manager or an advisor uses the results to make a fertiliser programme. It says which fertiliser, how much per tree, which blocks and when. You must follow this programme. Never add more because you think it will help. Too much fertiliser can burn roots, waste money and wash into rivers.

Types you may use

  • Granular fertiliser – small grains in bags, spread on the ground.
  • Fertiliser through the irrigation – mixed into the water. This is called fertigation.
  • Compost or manure – spread under the trees.
  • Leaf sprays – sprayed onto the leaves by trained sprayer teams.

Safety with fertiliser

  • Wear gloves, a dust mask, long sleeves and closed shoes.
  • Do not eat, drink or smoke while working with fertiliser.
  • Wash your hands and face before eating and at the end of the day.
  • If fertiliser gets in your eyes, rinse them with clean water for a long time and tell your supervisor.
  • Lift bags with your legs, not your back. Ask for help with heavy bags.

lessons.title: Spreading fertiliser correctly
lessons.html:
Applying granular fertiliser

Your supervisor gives you the block, the fertiliser type and the amount for each tree. Often you get a measuring cup or tin that holds the right amount.

Steps

  1. Check the bag. Make sure it is the fertiliser named on your instruction. If the name is different, stop and ask.
  2. Fill your bucket from the bag at the end of the row, not in the store.
  3. Use the measuring cup for every tree. Do not guess with your hand.
  4. Spread the fertiliser evenly in a ring under the outer edge of the canopy, where the feeding roots are. This is the drip line.
  5. Do not pile fertiliser against the stem. It can burn the bark.
  6. Do not throw fertiliser into drains, furrows or water.
  7. Count the trees you have done and the bags you have used.

Weather and timing

  • Spread when the soil is moist or before irrigation, so the fertiliser goes into the soil.
  • Do not spread before a big storm. Heavy rain can wash it away.
  • Follow the dates in the programme. Trees need food at certain times, for example before flowering and while nuts grow.

After the job

  • Close open bags and return them to the store. Keep the store dry and locked.
  • Sweep up spills and put them back in the bag or spread them in the orchard.
  • Rinse buckets and cups.
  • Give your supervisor the record: date, block, product, number of trees and bags used.

Key points

  • Fertiliser puts back the food that harvests take out.
  • Follow the fertiliser programme; never add extra.
  • Measure every tree and spread on the drip line, not against the stem.
  • Wear gloves and a mask, and wash before eating.
  • Record what you used and return bags to a dry, locked store.
